channel.title: Matt King: the thinking
channel.description: Weekly writing on what is going on in sport, marketing and culture.

item.title: The clipping economy
item.description: Most people never see a full match. They see a clip, cut by someone else and posted somewhere else. Sport can learn a lot from how streamers handle that.

item.title: Taylor Swift, the Chiefs and the side door
item.description: No campaign at all. Taylor Swift started turning up to watch Travis Kelce, and the broadcasts followed her. What it did, why it worked, and what to steal from it.

item.title: What Drive to Survive got right
item.description: F1 let the cameras into the paddock and handed the story to Netflix: the rivalries, the team bosses, the drivers as people. What it did, why it worked, and what to steal from it.

item.title: Baller League and the new format
item.description: Six-a-side football with its own rulebook, built for streams and short clips, with creators and famous faces in the dugouts. What it did, why it worked, and what to steal from it.

item.title: Alcaraz, Travis Scott and the drop
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz, tennis's It Boy, previewing Travis Scott's Nike tennis shoe. What it did, why it worked, and what to steal from it.

item.title: AI is the pit crew, not the driver
item.description: AI changes the tyres fast. It doesn't drive the car. How I use it in sports marketing, what it can't do yet, and why effort isn't the same as authenticity.
